summary: The note describes the State Council of the Soviet Union, formed on 5 September 1991 after the August 1991 coup attempt. It was intended as one of the most important government offices under Mikhail Gorbachev. Its members were the Soviet President and the top officials of the Soviet republics, typically their presidents. During the transition it was the highest organ of state power, with authority to elect a premier who could stand in for Gorbachev when absent.
one_line: The State Council of the USSR, formed in September 1991 after the August coup, was the highest state power organ during Gorbachev's transition.
key_facts: The State Council of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was formed on 5 September 1991.
The State Council was formed following the August 1991 Soviet coup d'état attempt.
The State Council was also known as the State Soviet.
The State Council was designed to be one of the most important government offices in Mikhail Gorbachev's Soviet Union.
The members of the State Council consisted of the President of the Soviet Union and the highest officials of the Soviet Union Republics.
The highest officials of the Soviet republics typically were presidents of their republics.
During the period of transition, the State Council was the highest organ of state power.
The State Council had the power to elect a premier, a person who would take Gorbachev's place if he was absent.
The office of Vice President of the Soviet Union had been abolished following the failed August Coup in 1991.
